record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: In GAN-based sharing of networked time-series datasets, can the generator support flexible notions of privacy in practice, and if so, under what training or generation configurations can those privacy notions be achieved?

evidence.quote: Natural questions arise: First, can GANs support these flexible notions of privacy in practice, and if so under what configurations?

artifact.category_tag: Generative adversarial networks for time-series privacy
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of releasing a synthetic version of a networked time-series dataset using a generative adversarial network (GAN). Formally, let $\mathcal{D} = \{(m_i, x_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ be a dataset where each record consists of a vector of metadata $m_i \in \mathcal{M}$ (e.g., per-object attributes) and an associated time series $x_i = (x_i^{(1)}, \dots, x_i^{(T)}) \in \mathcal{X}^T$. A GAN consists of a generator $G_\theta: \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{X}^T$ trained against a discriminator $D_\phi$ so that the induced distribution $P_{G_\theta}$ approximates the empirical distribution of $\mathcal{D}$.

A "flexible notion of privacy" refers to a family $\mathcal{P} = \{\Pi_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in A}$ of privacy specifications, where each $\Pi_\alpha$ may, for example, prescribe (i) a differential-privacy guarantee at level $(\varepsilon_\alpha, \delta_\alpha)$ for releasing $G_\theta$ or its samples, (ii) protection against membership inference for a specified subset of records, (iii) hiding of designated metadata attributes, or (iv) bounded leakage of designated time-series features, while preserving the joint distribution of the remaining attributes.

Determine whether there exist training procedures (loss functions, optimizers, noise-injection mechanisms, architectures) and sampling/generation configurations for $G_\theta$ such that, for a given specification $\Pi_\alpha \in \mathcal{P}$, the generator simultaneously (a) provably satisfies $\Pi_\alpha$ and (b) produces synthetic networked time-series samples whose statistical fidelity (in terms of marginal, temporal, and cross-record correlation metrics) is comparable to that of a non-private GAN trained on $\mathcal{D}$. Characterize the set of specifications $\Pi_\alpha$ for which such configurations exist, and describe explicit training/generation configurations achieving them.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning whether GANs can flexibly enforce diverse privacy notions when sharing networked time-series data. Subsequent work (e.g., DoppelGANger and follow-ups on differentially private time-series GANs) has explored differential-privacy training and selective attribute hiding, but no comprehensive characterization exists of which flexible privacy notions can be achieved with what configurations while retaining fidelity. The status is best described as open / actively researched.
